correctness.rationale: The six mixed differences suffice for submodularity, without monotonicity or normalization. Their rank-four image is cut out by equality of the three paired slack differences. With nonzero common difference only its lower side in each pair can be zero; with zero common difference zeros occur by whole pairs. Every such pattern is feasible, so there are 1+14+7=22. A fresh exact computation enumerated slack vectors in {0,1,2}^6 (enough for each feasible pattern by normalizing the nonzero difference to ±1) and built the projectors by rational Gram–Schmidt. It reproduced each class norm and the five maximal masks 15, 21, 42, 51, 60 with norm 7/4. For each face, its relative interior plus the normal cone's relative interior contains an open Euclidean projection region, on which the projection is the projector onto the face span. The closed face-plus-normal regions cover space and meet a segment in finitely many intervals; summing their bounds proves the global constant. At the sharp witness the residual is in the relative interior, not the ambient interior, of the normal cone (the wording in Step 4 is read with Step 2). The empty-set row is (5,2,2,−1,2,−1,−1,0)/8, so sufficiently small sign perturbations give equality. For one element the fit is unchanged; for two, the active half-space derivative I−aaᵀ/4 has norm 3/2 and is attained on an open region.
residual_risks: The face enumeration and sharp perturbation apply only to unweighted Euclidean regression on all eight coordinates. They say nothing about weighted, normalized, or larger submodular problems.

originality.rationale: The strongest indexed match is the same-day sharp coordinatewise modulus for weighted two-row supermodular regression. Its equal-weight m=4 case also gives 7/4 in eight coordinates, but it has three independent adjacent constraints and a five-dimensional lineality space, versus six constraints of rank four and four-dimensional lineality here. In particular these are not coordinate relabelings, sign changes or linearly equivalent cones. Its formula does not give the six-constraint face structure or directly imply the modulus for the three-element Boolean lattice. The prior convex-analytic face mechanism and baseline nonexpansiveness are standard; the supported distinct fact is the Boolean-lattice norm and face classification, not the method of polyhedral projection. No priority is inferred from the shared publication date or number.
residual_risks: Uninspected general projection results or exact finite tables under different set-function coordinates could contain an implication. One bounded web search and the local record comparisons do not certify absolute originality.
